results.title: Pyber's question on generators of abelian subgroups (Kourovka 20.75)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every prime $p$, every natural number $k$ and every finite $p$-group $G$, if every abelian normal subgroup of $G$ can be generated by at most $k$ elements, then every abelian subgroup of $G$ can be generated by at most $2k$ elements.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 20.75 has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 20.75 is false: there are a prime $p$, a natural number $k$, a finite $p$-group $G$ all of whose abelian normal subgroups can be generated by at most $k$ elements, and an abelian subgroup of $G$ that cannot be generated by at most $2k$ elements.

results.title: Pyber's question on orders of abelian subgroups (Kourovka 20.76)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every prime $p$, every natural number $k$ and every finite $p$-group $G$, if every abelian normal subgroup of $G$ has order at most $p^k$, then every abelian subgroup of $G$ has order at most $p^{2k}$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 20.76 has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 20.76 is false: there are a prime $p$, a natural number $k$, a finite $p$-group $G$ all of whose abelian normal subgroups have order at most $p^k$, and an abelian subgroup of $G$ of order greater than $p^{2k}$.

results.title: Hoffman word of a list of positive integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite list $(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of positive integers, this is the word $z_{k_1} z_{k_2} \cdots z_{k_r}$ in the free monoid on the two letters $x$ and $y$, where $z_k = x^{k-1} y$ is the Hoffman block of $k$. The empty list gives the empty word.

results.title: Words of $\mathfrak{H}^1$

results.title: The monoid of $\mathfrak{H}^0$-words

results.title: Polygonal numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $s$ and $n$, the $n$-th $s$-gonal number is $p_s(n) = (s - 2)\binom{n}{2} + n$, where $s - 2$ is truncated subtraction of natural numbers (so it is $0$ when $s < 2$).

results.title: Polygonal numbers at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $s$, $p_s(0) = 0$, where $p_s(n)$ is the $n$-th $s$-gonal number.

results.title: Polygonal numbers at one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $s$, $p_s(1) = 1$, where $p_s(n)$ is the $n$-th $s$-gonal number.

results.title: Polygonal numbers at two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $s \ge 3$, $p_s(2) = s$, where $p_s(n)$ is the $n$-th $s$-gonal number.

results.title: Polygonal numbers at three
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $s \ge 3$, $p_s(3) = 3s - 3$, where $p_s(n)$ is the $n$-th $s$-gonal number.

results.title: Polygonal numbers at four
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $s \ge 3$, $p_s(4) = 6s - 8$, where $p_s(n)$ is the $n$-th $s$-gonal number.

results.title: Closed form of the triangular numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the $n$-th triangular number is $p_3(n) = \frac{n(n + 1)}{2}$, where $p_s(n)$ is the $n$-th $s$-gonal number.

results.title: Square numbers as polygonal numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the $n$-th square number is $p_4(n) = n^2$, where $p_s(n)$ is the $n$-th $s$-gonal number.

results.title: Closed form of the pentagonal numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the $n$-th pentagonal number is $p_5(n) = \frac{3n^2 - n}{2}$, where $p_s(n)$ is the $n$-th $s$-gonal number.

results.title: Closed form of the hexagonal numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the $n$-th hexagonal number is $p_6(n) = 2n^2 - n$, where $p_s(n)$ is the $n$-th $s$-gonal number.

results.title: Statement of the Erdős–Mordell inequality
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Writing $XY$ for the distance between points $X$ and $Y$, this is the assertion that for all affinely independent points $A$, $B$, $C$ of the Euclidean plane, every point $P$ in the interior of the triangle $ABC$, and all points $M$, $N$, $L$ on the lines $BC$, $AB$, $CA$ such that the lines $PM$, $PN$, $PL$ are perpendicular to $BC$, $AB$, $CA$ respectively, we have $PA + PB + PC \ge 2(PM + PN + PL)$.

results.title: Erdős–Mordell inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be affinely independent points of the Euclidean plane and $P$ a point in the interior of the triangle $ABC$. Let $M$, $N$, $L$ be points on the lines $BC$, $AB$, $CA$ such that $PM \perp BC$, $PN \perp AB$ and $PL \perp CA$. Then, writing $XY$ for the distance between points $X$ and $Y$, we have $PA + PB + PC \ge 2(PM + PN + PL)$.

results.title: Functions bounded on a set
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A function $f : \beta \to \alpha$ into a space $\alpha$ with a bornology is bounded on a set $s \subseteq \beta$ if the image $f(s)$ is a bounded subset of $\alpha$.

results.title: Bounded functions
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A function $f : \beta \to \alpha$ into a space $\alpha$ with a bornology is bounded if its range $f(\beta)$ is a bounded subset of $\alpha$.

results.title: Hölder continuity
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be pseudo-extended metric spaces (distances take values in $[0, \infty]$), let $r \ge 0$ be a real number and $f : X \to Y$. Then $f$ is $r$-Hölder if there is a constant $C \ge 0$ such that $d_Y(f(x_1), f(x_2)) \le C \, d_X(x_1, x_2)^r$ for all $x_1, x_2 \in X$.

results.title: Hölder continuity on a set
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be pseudo-extended metric spaces (distances take values in $[0, \infty]$), let $r \ge 0$ be a real number, $s \subseteq X$ and $f : X \to Y$. Then $f$ is $r$-Hölder on $s$ if there is a constant $C \ge 0$ such that $d_Y(f(x_1), f(x_2)) \le C \, d_X(x_1, x_2)^r$ for all $x_1, x_2 \in s$.

results.title: Continuously differentiable functions with Hölder derivative
results.caption: Definition

A function $f : E \to F$ is in $C^{1,\alpha}(E)$ if $f$ is continuously differentiable over $\mathbb{k}$ and its derivative $Df$, a map from $E$ to the space $L(E, F)$ of continuous $\mathbb{k}$-linear maps with the operator norm, is bounded and $\alpha$-Hölder.

results.title: Spatial directional derivative of a time-dependent vector field
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given $u, v : \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$, the spatial directional derivative $(u \cdot \nabla_x) v$ of $v$ in the direction of $u$ is the function $(x, t) \mapsto D_x v(x, t)\,[u(x, t)]$, where $D_x v(x, t)$ is the Fréchet derivative of $y \mapsto v(y, t)$ at $x$ (taken to be $0$ if this map is not differentiable at $x$).

results.title: Time derivative
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $u(x, t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$ of a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and a time $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the time derivative $\partial_t u(x, t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the derivative at $t$ of the function $s \mapsto u(x, s)$, taken to be $0$ when that function is not differentiable at $t$.

results.title: Spatial gradient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $p(x, t)$ of a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and a time $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the spatial gradient $\nabla_x p(x, t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the gradient at $x$ of the function $y \mapsto p(y, t)$, taken to be $0$ when that function is not differentiable at $x$.

results.title: Divergence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The divergence of a vector field $u : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ at a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the trace of the Fréchet derivative $Du(x)$, a linear map from $\mathbb{R}^3$ to $\mathbb{R}^3$ (taken to be $0$ if $u$ is not differentiable at $x$).

results.title: Standard basis vectors of ℝ³
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, $e_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the $i$-th standard basis vector: its $i$-th coordinate is $1$ and its other coordinates are $0$.

results.title: Vorticity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The vorticity of a vector field $u : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is its curl $(\nabla \times u)(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{3} e_i \times Du(x)\,e_i$, where $e_1, e_2, e_3$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$, $\times$ is the cross product and $Du(x)\,e_i$ is the partial derivative of $u$ at $x$ in direction $e_i$ (all taken to be $0$ when $u$ is not differentiable at $x$).

results.title: Odd vector fields in three dimensions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A vector field $u : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with components $u_1, u_2, u_3$ is odd if, for each $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, the component $u_i$ is an odd function of the $i$-th coordinate and an even function of each of the other two coordinates, when the remaining coordinates are held fixed.

results.title: Regular Cayley graph
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a group $G$ and a natural number $k$, the data of a $k$-regular Cayley graph on $G$ is a finite set $S \subseteq G$ of generators such that $S$ is closed under inverses ($s \in S$ implies $s^{-1} \in S$), the identity $1$ does not belong to $S$, every element of $G$ is the product of a finite (possibly empty) list of elements of $S$, and $S$ has exactly $k$ elements.

results.title: First-return probability
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a $k$-regular Cayley graph on a group $G$ with generating set $S$. For $n \ge 1$, the first-return probability of $\Gamma$ at time $n$ is the real number obtained by dividing by $k^n$ the number of words $(s_1, \dots, s_n) \in S^n$ with $s_1 s_2 \cdots s_n = 1$ and $s_1 \cdots s_m \ne 1$ for every $0 < m < n$; at time $n = 0$ it is $0$.

results.title: Return probability
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The return probability of a $k$-regular Cayley graph $\Gamma$ is the sum $\sum_{n \ge 0} p_n$, where $p_n$ is the first-return probability of $\Gamma$ at time $n$.

results.title: Uniform return-probability gap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every natural number $k > 1$ there is a real number $C < 1$ such that for every group $G$ and every $k$-regular Cayley graph $\Gamma$ on $G$, if the return probability of $\Gamma$ is less than $1$ (that is, $\Gamma$ is transient), then it is at most $C$.

results.title: Uniform return-probability gap for transient Cayley graphs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k > 1$ there is a real number $C < 1$ such that for every group $G$ and every $k$-regular Cayley graph $\Gamma$ on $G$ whose return probability is less than $1$, the return probability of $\Gamma$ is at most $C$.

results.title: Sidon subsets of $\{1, \dots, N\}$
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Largest Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ (Erdős Problem 861)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $N$, $f(N)$ is the largest cardinality of a Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 861, first question
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A(N)$ be the number of Sidon subsets of $\{1, \dots, N\}$, including the empty set and the singletons, and let $f(N)$ be the largest size of a Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$. The statement is that $A(N) / 2^{f(N)} \to \infty$ as $N \to \infty$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 861, second question
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A(N)$ be the number of Sidon subsets of $\{1, \dots, N\}$, including the empty set and the singletons, and let $f(N)$ be the largest size of a Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$. The statement is that $\log_2 A(N) / f(N) \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$, that is, $A(N) = 2^{(1 + o(1)) f(N)}$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 861, first question: positive answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A(N)$ be the number of Sidon subsets of $\{1, \dots, N\}$, including the empty set and the singletons, and let $f(N)$ be the largest size of a Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$. Then $A(N) / 2^{f(N)} \to \infty$ as $N \to \infty$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 861, second question: negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A(N)$ be the number of Sidon subsets of $\{1, \dots, N\}$, including the empty set and the singletons, and let $f(N)$ be the largest size of a Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$. Then the ratio $\log_2 A(N) / f(N)$ does not tend to $1$ as $N \to \infty$; that is, $A(N) = 2^{(1 + o(1)) f(N)}$ fails.

results.title: Least common multiple of the parts of a partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a partition $p$ of $n$, this is the least common multiple of the parts of $p$, taken with the convention that it equals $1$ when $p$ has no parts.

results.title: Landau's function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, Landau's function at $n$ is the maximum, over all partitions $p$ of $n$, of the least common multiple of the parts of $p$.

results.title: The Landau function bounds the LCM of the parts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every partition $p$ of $n$, the least common multiple of the parts of $p$ is at most the Landau function at $n$.

results.title: The Landau function is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, some partition of $n$ has least common multiple of its parts equal to the Landau function at $n$.

results.summary: Padding the finite state sets preserves the full sum of vertex weights and arbitrary pair kernels. No factorization, finiteness of the state carriers, or global injectivity is required.

results.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher transition matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The neutral Wright–Fisher transition matrix on `M` gene copies (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): `P(i, j) = (M choose j) (i/M)^j (1 - i/M)^(M - j)`, the binomial law `Bin(M, i/M)` of the number of `A` copies among `M` draws with replacement. The model needs `M ≥ 1`; for `M = 0` (where `i / M` is Lean's junk value `0`) the matrix is the one-state chain, which is `Bin(0, p) = δ₀` for every `p`.

results.title: Allele frequency of a Wright–Fisher state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The frequency of allele `A` in state `i` is `bernstein.z i = i / M` (for `M = 0` it is Lean's junk value `i / 0 = 0`).

results.title: Entries of the Wright–Fisher matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Entries of the Wright–Fisher matrix.

results.title: Heterozygosity of a Wright–Fisher state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The heterozygosity `H(j) = 2 (j/M) (1 - j/M)` of state `j`: the probability that two gene copies drawn with replacement carry different alleles.

results.title: Wright–Fisher rows are binomial laws
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The rows of the Wright–Fisher matrix are Mathlib's binomial laws `Bin(M, i/M)`.

results.title: One-step martingale property of the Wright–Fisher allele count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Martingale property of the allele count (one step): `∑ j, P(i, j) j = i`.

results.title: Multi-step martingale property of the Wright–Fisher allele count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Martingale property of the allele count (`t` steps): `∑ j, P^t(i, j) j = i`.

results.title: Loss of an allele is absorbing in the Wright–Fisher chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The state `0` (allele `A` lost) is absorbing.

results.title: Fixation of an allele is absorbing in the Wright–Fisher chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The state `M` (allele `A` fixed) is absorbing.

results.title: One-step decay of heterozygosity under Wright–Fisher drift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Heterozygosity decays by the factor `1 - 1/M` per generation (one step). For `M = 0` both sides are `0` because `H ≡ 0`.

results.title: Geometric decay of heterozygosity under Wright–Fisher drift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Heterozygosity decays geometrically (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): `∑ j, P^t(i, j) H(j) = (1 - 1/M)^t H(i)`. For `M = 0` both sides are `0` because `H ≡ 0` (the factor `1 - 1/0 = 1` is then irrelevant).

results.title: Interior Wright–Fisher states vanish in the limit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The probability of sitting in an interior state `0 < j < M` at time `t` tends to `0`.

results.title: Fixation probability in the Wright–Fisher chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fixation probability (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): started from `i` copies, allele `A` is fixed with limiting probability `i / M`, i.e. `P^t(i, M) → i / M`.

results.title: Limiting loss probability of the Wright–Fisher transition matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Loss probability: started from `i` copies, allele `A` is lost with limiting probability `1 - i / M`, i.e. `P^t(i, 0) → 1 - i / M`.

results.title: Limiting fixation probability of a Wright–Fisher chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Path-level fixation probability: if `X` is a Wright–Fisher chain (in the sense of `IsFiniteMarkovChain`) started from `i` copies, then `P(X_t = M) → i / M`.

results.title: Almost-sure absorption of the Wright–Fisher chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Almost-sure absorption: a Wright–Fisher chain is almost surely eventually absorbed in `0` or `M` (Ewens 2004, ch. 3).

results.title: Fixation probability of a Wright–Fisher chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Path-level fixation probability (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): a Wright–Fisher chain started from `i` copies ever reaches `M` (fixation of `A`) with probability `i / M`.

results.title: Loss probability of a Wright–Fisher chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Path-level loss probability: a Wright–Fisher chain started from `i` copies ever reaches `0` (loss of `A`) with probability `1 - i / M`.

results.title: Finite Wright–Fisher chain is absorbed almost surely
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The finite Wright–Fisher chain under the canonical Markov law almost surely reaches an endpoint. The law and chain are not premises supplied by a caller.

results.title: Fixation probability of the finite Wright–Fisher chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under the canonical finite Wright–Fisher law, the probability of ever fixing at `M` equals the initial allele frequency `i / M`.

results.title: Loss probability of an allele in the finite Wright–Fisher chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under the canonical finite Wright–Fisher law, the probability of ever losing the allele at `0` equals `1 - i / M`.
